                    ### Question
                    In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o.
opb. Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.
opc. Cyclophosphamide i.v. 1 g / m2.
opd. Infliximab i.v. 3 mg / Kg.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, prolonged morning stiffness, and unilateral bruising, there is a strong suspicion of giant cell arteritis (GCA) or polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) with possible systemic involvement. High-dose corticosteroids are indicated as a first-line treatment to prevent complications such as vision loss associated with GCA. The reasoning for Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days aligns with the consensus that immediate high-dose corticosteroid therapy is warranted in suspected GCA. Prednisone 10 mg daily is less aggressive and may not be sufficient for urgent cases. Cyclophosphamide is not indicated as an initial treatment for GCA or PMR, and Infliximab is not first-line therapy before confirming the diagnosis. Therefore, the best option is Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.
